title: CLI traces delete --trace-ids: strip whitespace around each comma-separated trace ID before deleting
answers: Why does mlflow traces delete leave some traces behind when I pass several trace IDs separated by commas and spaces?
How do I pass multiple trace IDs to traces delete from the command line, and does the space after each comma matter?
Where is the --trace-ids parsing for the traces delete command handled?
Does the MCP delete_traces tool accept trace IDs written as 'a, b' with a space after the comma?
body:
Path: `mlflow traces delete` CLI (`mlflow/cli/traces.py:delete_traces`) takes an experiment id plus either a comma-separated `--trace-ids` list or max-timestamp/max-traces filters, and passes the parsed IDs to `TracingClient.delete_traces`. The same command backs the MCP `delete_traces` tool.
Rule: Split comma-separated ID options with a strip per entry, e.g. `[t.strip() for t in trace_ids.split(",")] if trace_ids else None`, as `traces search --order-by` and `traces evaluate --trace-ids` already do. Without the strip, `" tr-2"` reaches the store, matches no trace, and is silently skipped.
Symptom: A user ran `mlflow traces delete --trace-ids "tr-1, tr-2"`; the command exited 0 and printed a smaller deleted count, and `tr-2` was still present in `traces search` afterward.
Constraints: Applies to comma-split ID options on trace CLI commands. `mlflow gc --run-ids/--experiment-ids` does not strip, but it fails loudly with a not-found error, so it was left unchanged. Regression test asserts the exact IDs passed to `delete_traces` (`tests/cli/test_traces.py:test_delete_command_strips_spaces_in_trace_ids`), since the exit code alone does not catch this.
applies: Any CLI option that takes a comma-separated list of trace IDs and forwards them to the tracing store.
says: Deleting multiple traces with spaces after commas leaves some traces behind.
Batch trace deletion silently skips records if the input list contains spaces.
Allow spaces after commas when providing multiple record identifiers for removal.
Command line trace cleanup should ignore whitespace around comma separated identifiers.
search: `mlflow traces delete` in mlflow/cli/traces.py (and the backing MCP delete_traces tool) must strip whitespace around each comma-separated entry parsed from --trace-ids before passing them to TracingClient.delete_traces. Without stripping, leading or trailing whitespace causes IDs to silently miss matches in the trace store. This rule applies to comma-separated trace ID CLI options, matching behavior in traces search --order-by and traces evaluate --trace-ids. In contrast, mlflow gc --run-ids/--experiment-ids does not strip whitespace because it fails loudly on not-found errors.
